newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot MTBE sags on bearish factors.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot MTBE sags on bearish factors.

text.p: U.S. spot MTBE prices sagged nearly five cents this week under the weight of bearish factors, including the return of Iraqi oil to the market, players said on Thursday.
A 1.5 million barrel build in reformulated gasoline in the week and a conference today and Friday in New York for MTBE players added to the decline in values.
"There was just nothing today," said one U.S. trader. "Prices have been slipping for the past two days."

On the Gulf Coast, Houston spot MTBE fell about 4.00 cents to between 83.00 cents and 84.25 cents in a market scarce of buyers. Houston January material was pegged 2.25 cents lower from last Thursday at 84.25/85.25 cents.
New York spot MTBE also slipped 2.50 cents to 88.00/89.00 cents in quiet trade, players said.
There may however be an uptick in prices further in the month due to a cutback in production by a few MTBE producers.
ENRON confirmed rumors earlier Thursday that it has scaled back output, but declined to give production details.
"We have been curtailing production in the last week and will continue to evaluate that decision based on the economics of making MTBE," said one ENRON source.
-- Laney Salisbury New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
